column2: City of the Damned

In the year 1999 the twin-tailed comet fell on Mordheim, and the City of the Damned has been a charnel house ever since, its ruins thick with wyrdstone worth more than its weight in gold. The plans to take a share of it are coming together, but someone must lead the work. A commander could take an army to seize a county of the ruined city, or a sly agent could slip into the ruins with a warband and bring the stone home. Who will you choose?
I will send a skilled commander.
I will send a skilled agent.
I will hire a captain to lead the expedition.
There is no one fit for this. Call it off.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has chosen you to go to Mordheim, the City of the Damned, where the comet fell and the green stone lies thick among the ruins. Every fool with a sword is going there: Reiklanders and Middenheimers, Marienburgers with their deep purses, the Sisters of Sigmar, cultists, ratmen and worse. Few come back. You must leave at once.
To Mordheim, then.

The expeditionary force sent to Mordheim has reached the outskirts of the ruins and dug in. From the camp they can see the shattered spires and the green glow beneath them. They are ready to fight for their share of the stone.
Let's hope they succeed.

Your agent [mordheim_agent.GetTitledFirstName] has slipped into the ruins of Mordheim, where [mordheim_agent.GetSheHe] will try to seize some of the precious wyrdstone on your behalf, among the warbands, the cultists and things that are worse.
No word has come from Mordheim. Your agent is dead, and whatever stone [mordheim_agent.GetSheHe] found lies in some other pocket now.
Let's hope [mordheim_agent.GetSheHe] gets results.
The City of the Damned has taken another.
Your agent in Mordheim has made no progress in finding wyrdstone.
Your agent in Mordheim has made no real progress in finding wyrdstone, but swears that with more coin for bribes and blades [From.GetSheHe] will surely have stone for you within a year.
Your agent in Mordheim has been slain in the streets of the City of the Damned, by a monster, a rival warband or the stone itself. Somewhere a scavenger is going through [From.GetHerHis] pockets.
Curses!
Fine. You had better deliver!
Better to recall [From.GetHerHim].
Disappointing. Back to work.
Your agent has come back from Mordheim with a share of the precious wyrdstone, wrapped in lead and wax, to use as you see fit. [From.GetSheHe] does not speak much of what [From.GetSheHe] saw.
Splendid.
Your captain in Mordheim, [mordheim_agent.GetTitledFirstName], has sent you plunder found in the cursed city, to fill your store of wyrdstone.
The City of the Damned pays well.
The Mists Lift

Since the comet fell, a mist has hung over the ruins of Mordheim and the lands around it, and armies that marched into it were lost. Now travellers say the mist is thinning, and the warbands are leaving. The easy stone is gone, the Pit is quiet, and the race for the City of the Damned is over. Its lands lie open to any lord with the swords to take them, and in the shadow markets wyrdstone grows scarce and dear.
Mordheim is open.
Miners in [Root.GetName] have struck a vein of strange greenish-black rock. The peasants call it wyrdstone, for the wondrous and dreadful things that happen around it. How should we deal with it?
Interesting. Leave it be.
We must act fast and take it for ourselves!
Quickly, send for the witch hunters!

A burning green star has fallen out of the sky near [Root.GetName]. Those who saw it say it came from Morrslieb, the Chaos moon. Where it struck, the earth is scorched and the rock glows: wyrdstone, a great deal of it.
Interesting. Leave it be.
It shall be mine!
Quickly, send for the witch hunters!
A Green Star Falls
A burning green star was seen to fall from Morrslieb into the lands of [From.GetTitledName]. Where it struck, they say, the rock glows.
An ill omen.
Green Treasure
The wyrdstone mine in [From.GetName] has brought up another year's yield of stone for you, wrapped in lead and carried up by miners who no longer sleep well.
It belongs to me now.
Our wyrdstone mine in [Root.GetName] is exhausted. The last of the stone has been swept up as dust, and the miners say there is nothing left to dig.
Nothing left at all?
Shadowy Market

After several days, your go-betweens have made contact with the Wyrdstone Emporium. They bring in a hooded figure who smells faintly of sewers. While the warbands of Mordheim flood the market, stone is cheap.\n\nThe figure asks you: Sell-give or buy-take?
I am here to sell wyrdstone.
I wish to buy wyrdstone.
Never mind.
The bigger the stone, the better the price-gold you get for selling it.
Some dust (60 gold).
A shard (150 gold).
A cluster (250 gold).
The bigger the stone, the more price-gold you pay for buying it.
Some dust (80 gold).
A shard (200 gold).
A cluster (320 gold).

After several days, your go-betweens have made contact with the Wyrdstone Emporium. They bring in a hooded figure who smells faintly of sewers. Since the mists over Mordheim lifted, stone is scarce, and the price-gold has gone up.\n\nThe figure asks you: Sell-give or buy-take?
Some dust (100 gold).
A shard (250 gold).
A cluster (400 gold).
Some dust (130 gold).
A shard (300 gold).
A cluster (480 gold).
Whispers of Wyrdstone

Your spymaster tells you that there is talk at court and in the taverns: that hooded men come and go by the postern gate, that your coffers ring with ratmen's gold, that you keep a box of green stone in your chambers. Possession of wyrdstone is forbidden by the law and the temples alike. A few silver coins in the right hands would quiet it.
Pay them to forget.
Let them talk.
Seal it away, where no one can reach it.
Seal it away, where no one can reach it.

The wyrdstone mine in [From.GetName] has brought up another year's yield. Your stores are full, or you have no use for the stuff, so the hooded agents of the Wyrdstone Emporium who wait at the mine head have bought it on the spot, in gold that smells faintly of sewers.
The yield is sold to the shadow market
Stone is lost from the mine
Something in the ruins
Your capital is within reach of Mordheim (Skaven tunnel under it from anywhere)
Ratmen Beneath

The overseer of the mine in [From.GetName] comes to you pale and shaking. The lower galleries have broken into tunnels no man dug, round and smooth and stinking of wet fur. Stone has been going missing for months, and last night three miners did not come up. The miners say they heard chittering in the dark, and saw red eyes.
Bring the galleries down on them.
Send armed men into the dark.
Leave them a shard of stone and let them be.
The Miners Sicken

The miners of [From.GetName] are sick. They cough up green phlegm, their gums bleed, and their teeth fall out. Some have grown sores that will not heal, and in the village a child was born with a third eye and was drowned in the millpond. The priests say the mine is cursed. The overseer asks for coin to send the sick away and bring in fresh hands.
Pay for fresh miners (50 gold).
Work them until they drop.
The Pit

A message from [From.GetTitledFirstName] in Mordheim: [From.GetSheHe] has found a way down to the Pit, the crater where the comet struck. The stone lies there in great glowing clusters, more than all the warbands have found in a year. But the Pit is the lair of the Possessed, who keep their vigil for the Shadowlord, and the air itself is poison. [From.GetSheHe] awaits your word.
Go down into the Pit.
Not even for wyrdstone. Come away.
A Rival Warband

Your agent [From.GetTitledFirstName] writes that a rival warband has found a cache of wyrdstone in a cellar off the Merchants' Quarter. They are few, they are drunk on their luck, and they are watching the street. [From.GetSheHe] could fall on them at night, offer them coin for the stone, or slip away and keep looking.
Fall on them. The stone is ours.
Buy it from them.
Let them have it. There is more.
The Sisters of Sigmar

The Sisters of Sigmar have taken your agent [From.GetTitledFirstName]. The warrior-nuns of the Rock, the convent on its island in the Stir, gather the cursed stone to seal it away from the world, and they have no love for those who would sell it. They write that the prisoner may be ransomed, if [From.GetSheHe] is not judged a heretic first. They do not write how heretics are judged, but everyone knows.

Your agent [From.GetTitledFirstName] has met the Sisters of Sigmar, the warrior-nuns of the Rock, the convent on its island in the Stir. They gather the cursed stone to seal it away from the world, in the name of the Heldenhammer. The Matriarch asks that you, as one of the faithful of Sigmar, give them the stone your agent has gathered, and promises the prayers of the whole Sisterhood.
Give it to them, in Sigmar's name.
Pay the ransom (75 gold).
Let them burn [From.GetHerHim].
The Possessed

Your agent [From.GetTitledFirstName] writes less often now, and the letters are strange. [From.GetSheHe] writes that the cultists of the Possessed came to [From.GetHerHim] in the night, near the Pit, and spoke of the Shadowlord, and of what the stone could make of a mortal who did not fear it. [From.GetSheHe] writes that [From.GetSheHe] sent them away. The hand is shakier than before.

Your agent [From.GetTitledFirstName] writes that the cultists of the Possessed, who keep their vigil for the Shadowlord at the Pit, have heard of you. They know a servant of the Dark Gods when they see one, and they have sent a gift of kinship: a shard of the purest stone, warm to the touch.
The gods reward their own.
[From.GetSheHe] is still useful. Let [From.GetHerHim] work on.
Bring [From.GetHerHim] home, and watch [From.GetHerHim] closely.
A Relic of the Old City

In the ruins of a temple, under a fallen roof and the bones of the templars who died defending it, your agent [From.GetTitledFirstName] has found a fine old sword, its blade still bright and its hilt set with a blessing of the old city. It was meant to be carried by a hero. Mordheim was not kind to heroes.
It shall hang at my side.
Sell it (150 gold).
Give it back to the Church of Sigmar.
